Operator:
Good morning, and welcome to the AeroTech Dynamics Third Quarter Fiscal 2024 Earnings Conference Call. All participants will be in listen-only mode. After today's presentation, there will be an opportunity to ask questions. As a reminder, instructions for queuing up will be given at that time. Please note this event is being recorded.

I would now like to turn the conference over to Sarah Thompson, Vice President of Investor Relations. Please go ahead.

Sarah Thompson:
Thank you, Operator, and good morning, everyone. Welcome to AeroTech Dynamics' Third Quarter Fiscal 2024 Earnings Conference Call. Joining me today are David Larson, Chief Executive Officer; Emily Carter, Chief Financial Officer; Robert Kline, Chief Operating Officer; Dr. Sofia Reyes, Chief Technology Officer; Mark Donovan, Chief Strategy Officer; Laura Jenkins, Chief Marketing Officer; and Kevin Walsh, Chief Compliance Officer.

Before we begin, I'd like to remind you that this call contains forward-looking statements within the meaning of the safe harbor provisions of the Private Securities Litigation Reform Act of 1995. Actual results may differ materially from those discussed. Please refer to our SEC filings, including our most recent Form 10-K and 10-Q, for a complete discussion of risks and uncertainties.

David Larson:
Thank you, Sarah, and good morning. AeroTech Dynamics delivered a solid performance in the third quarter, demonstrating the resilience of our business model and the strength of our diversified portfolio across defense, commercial aviation, space, and advanced systems. Our priorities remain focused on executing our strategy, driving operational excellence, and delivering long-term value to our shareholders. We posted record quarterly revenue of $8.7 billion, up 14% year-over-year and 3% above our guidance midpoint, with adjusted EPS at $2.45, surpassing consensus by $0.12. This was driven by favorable program mix, cost discipline, and higher-than-expected volume in defense.

Key highlights include standout new business wins, a favorable defense budget environment, accelerating commercial aircraft deliveries, robust aftermarket growth from rising fleet utilization and maintenance cycles, supportive geopolitical dynamics boosting spending, exceptional execution on priority defense programs, and clear strategic priorities setting us up for continued growth. We're particularly excited about the recent advancements in our Dark Eagle hypersonic weapon program and its potential to revolutionize long-range precision strike capabilities, fueling our future growth trajectory. Demand for our defense systems remains strong, while our commercial aerospace business continues its steady recovery.

I'll now turn it over to Emily for a deeper dive into our financial results and these key areas.

Emily Carter:
Thank you, David. Now, let's turn to the financials. In the third quarter, we reported revenue of $8.7 billion, representing a 14% increase year-over-year. Our adjusted earnings per share were $2.45. We continue to maintain a strong balance sheet with $4.1 billion in cash and equivalents and $12 billion in total liquidity. Our guidance for the full fiscal year remains unchanged at the high end, reflecting active cost management and investments in key growth initiatives. We're also focused on returning capital to shareholders through dividends and share repurchases, including $500 million in buybacks this quarter and a 12% dividend increase to $0.65 per share.

Specific financial highlights include gross margins of 25.2%, operating income of $1.3 billion, and free cash flow of $1.2 billion, up 30% year-over-year. Adjusted EBITDA margins expanded 150 basis points to 15.4%. Company-wide, our funded backlog hit a record $142 billion, up 15% year-over-year, providing visibility through 2028 with 40% international exposure and a book-to-bill of 1.3x.

Let me provide more color on the major drivers. First, on major new contract awards and program wins: We had an exceptionally strong quarter for new business at AeroTech Dynamics, reporting record contract awards totaling $12.4 billion, up 28% year-over-year and our highest quarterly total since the NGAD downselect in 2022. This lifts our funded backlog to $148 billion—a 15% increase from Q2—and total backlog, including unfunded, to over $285 billion. Our book-to-bill ratio reached 1.45x, highlighting the strength of our pipeline amid rising global defense spending.

Breaking it down: On fixed-wing platforms, we secured a $4.2 billion full-rate production contract from the U.S. Air Force for Lot 16 and Lot 17 F-35 Lightning II airframes and mission systems integration, including Block 4 upgrades with enhanced sensor fusion, AI-driven electronic warfare suites, and TR-3 engine enhancements for better thrust-to-weight ratios. As a Tier 1 supplier partnering with Lockheed Martin, this sustains the program's 1,200+ global fleet, with accretive margins of 12-14% thanks to our proprietary composites reducing lifecycle costs by 18% per airframe versus legacy materials.

In hypersonics—a market we see growing at 25% CAGR through 2030—we captured a $2.8 billion IDIQ from the U.S. Army's Rapid Capabilities office for the Dark Eagle ground-launched hypersonic weapon, covering LRIP through FY27 with boost-glide vehicles at Mach 5+ and 1,725 nautical mile ranges. Our edge stems from scramjet inlets and thermal protection systems tested at our Mojave facility, offering 30% superior heat dissipation. Early options add $1.1 billion to funded backlog.

Missile defense saw a $1.9 billion FMS contract via the State Department for Next Generation Interceptor boost-phase kill vehicles for Poland's Aegis Ashore under the European Phased Adaptive Approach, aligning with NATO's post-Ukraine deterrence and a 35% EPAA uptick. Our exo-atmospheric vehicle features gallium nitride AESA radars and hit-to-kill thrusters with 99.7% intercept probability in simulations, edging out Raytheon.

Internationally, a $1.5 billion sustainment package for Australia's F/A-18E/F Super Hornets under AUKUS Pillar 1 includes CCA drone wingman integration with our MQ-Next UAVs—Australia now 8% of international backlog amid their $368 billion recap. In the Middle East, $1.2 billion from UAE for Patriot PAC-3 MSE and David's Sling co-production marks our first regional IP-sharing win, with 20-year annuities amid Houthi threats.

Emerging tech added $700 million in space contracts, like Space Force GPS IIIF and DARPA Blackjack LEO demos, using silicon carbide photonics for resilient PNT with 95% radiation-hardened yields—bookings up 45% YoY on the $18 billion Space Force budget.

These wins de-risk us: 60% multi-year fixed-price with CPI escalators shielding inflation (steel/titanium +22%). FMS now 22% of awards, cutting U.S. DoD risk. Digital twins shortened proposals 25%. Pipeline of $45 billion for H2 includes hypersonic follow-ons, B-21 subsystems, GCAP bids. With budgets at 2.4% global GDP and U.S. FY25 at $886 billion, we guide $48-52 billion FY24 awards for low-teens EPS growth and 18% ROIC by 2026.

Shifting to the defense budget outlook and its impact: The FY25 NDAA passed with $895 billion DoD topline, up 4.5% YoY and fourth straight real growth above inflation—procurement +6.2% to $167 billion, RDT&E +8.1% to $145 billion. Munitions replenishment via Ukraine aid adds $28 billion for PrSM, JASSM-ERs, Glide Phase Interceptors. Fixed-wing steady at $62 billion for F-35/NGAD; rotary +12% for UH-60M/CH-47F.

This benefits our 68% U.S. gov revenue, backlog $42.7 billion up 14% YoY at 1.28x book-to-bill. Missiles ramp to 650 JASSM annually, $2.8 billion FY25 awards from $4.2 billion MYP. F-35/NGAD composites $1.1 billion follow-on, margins to 14.2%. Space up 22% on SDA Tranche 3.

Internationally (22% revenue, 30% backlog), NATO to $1.4 trillion in 2025 +11%—Germany's €100 billion fund for F-35/ECRS Mk2; Poland HIMARS/Abrams with our PGKs; Middle East FMS $50 billion/year for Iron Dome/THAAD, +19% Q3. Asia: Japan GCAP XA102 engines; AUKUS AUD 3 billion hypersonics; Pacific Deterrence $9.1 billion.

Impact: Raising FY25 revenue to $18.9-$19.3 billion (+9-11%), EPS $12.85-$13.15 (+12%), margins +220bps to 13.8%. From F-35 ALIS/ODIN $1.2 billion recurring; CCA autonomy 16% margins; 95% domestic titanium. Hypersonics $450 million Q3 R&D for Mayhem/HAWC; ATLAS C4ISR; HELIOS lasers $800 million. JVs in Turkey/India for 15% share growth. ROIC 18.2% vs. peers. FY26 revenue +10-12%, EPS 13-15% CAGR.

On commercial aircraft delivery rates and recovery: Our Commercial Airplanes division delivered 142 aircraft in Q3, +28% YoY and +15% sequential, on track for 520-570 full-year. Pre-COVID 45/month average; pandemic low 157/year; now 38/month, narrowbodies (737 MAX 31/month) +8% over 2019, widebodies ramping to 8-10/month.

Backlog $528 billion (5,200 aircraft, 65% narrowbody), list prices +12% to $145 million. RPKs 102% of 2019, narrowbody utilization 95%. North America 35% deliveries (Delta/United 737s); Europe 25% (Ryanair/Lufthansa); APAC 28% (IndiGo/ANA, China delays 15 units); ME/LATAM 12%.

Invested $2.1 billion supply chain, 80% dual-sourced forgings; factories 85% automated, 737 cycles -22% to 14 days; 787 additive nacelles -50% lead times; LEAP yields 98%. 40% SAF-capable. Defense $92 billion backlog stabilizes costs at 72% absorption; inventory 185 days; hedges $450 million.

Ahead: 45-50/month 2025, widebody 12/month on 777X cert; 7,000-unit pipeline for mid-teens EBITDA.

Drivers of aftermarket performance: $2.8 billion revenue +18% YoY, 42% total top-line, EBITDA 32.5% (+250bps). Commercial traffic 105% 2019, ASK +12%; narrowbody 11.2 hours/day (+1.4); LEAP cycles 4,200 (+400). Defense FHL 1.2 million +14%, F-35 22% share; rotary +20%.

Maintenance +22% C/D checks (1,450 events); narrowbody age 12+ years; APAC +30% line maint. AeroDef Digital -15% unscheduled. North America 45% growth (92% capacity); EMEA +25% (PMA $180 million); APAC +16%; LatAm +8%.

$500 million additive -40% F-35 repairs; HealthHub 65% base. FY24 +15-17%, mid-teens margins; 75% composites integration.

Geopolitical factors: Global spend $2.44 trillion +6.8%, top 15 at 82%. U.S. FY25 $895 billion +4.1%, NGAD $2.7 billion, Columbia LRIP $3.5 billion; F-35 sustain $2.1 billion +22%; SM-6 $1.8 billion.

Europe: NATO +18% since 2014, 23/32 at 2%; Ukraine $175 billion—Javelin 1,200 YTD, Patriot GEM-T sold to 2028 ($4.2 billion). APAC: AUKUS $10 billion, Japan F-35/Tomahawk $2.9 billion, Australia Ghost Bat. ME: Israel aid $14.5 billion PGMs +35%; GCC $120 billion C4ISR.

$4.2 billion IR&D; FY25 bookings $45 billion, margins 12.5%; EPS +8-10%, ROIC >15%.

Performance of priority defense programs: $2.8 billion +18% YoY, 62% segment, margins 14.8% (+220bps), backlog $52 billion ($28 billion funded). NGAD LRIP Lot 4 early, 14 aircraft $1.1 billion +25%, intl $2.4 billion Block 3; hypersonics $650 million +42%, AGM-XYZ Mach 5+ IOC FY25, $900 million bookings; IAMD $850 million +15%, 180 interceptors 98% success, $1.2 billion HGV; uncrewed/space $200 million +35%, CCA $400 million, SDA 95% availability.

Dual-sourcing 85%; $450 million capex. FY24 $11-11.5 billion, 14-15% margins.

Strategic priorities and outlook: Funded backlog $182 billion +15%, 5.5 years visibility, book-to-bill 1.3x, $11.2 billion awards incl. $2.8 billion F-35 Lot 16, $1.5 billion HIMARS. Q4 revenue $8.7-9.0 billion +10-13% QoQ, margins 11.5-12.0%, FCF $1.2-1.5 billion, EPS $2.85-3.05. FY25 revenue $35.5-36.5 billion +11-14%, EPS $12.50-13.00 +9-13%, margins 12.2-12.5%. Aeronautics $16-16.5 billion +13%, CCA $800 million SBIR TRL-6 mid-2025 with ML swarm tactics akin to DARPA's ACE program.

With that comprehensive review, I'll hand it back for operational insights.

Robert Kline:
Thank you, Emily. Operationally, we've made significant supply chain improvements, increasing production rates on key programs like F-35 and hypersonics. Investments in automation and digital technologies, including our V-LEAN initiative and digital twins, have boosted efficiency, cutting F-35 wing cycles by 22% and de-risking titanium sourcing to 95% domestic. We've achieved 95% on-time deliveries and navigated inflation through dual-sourcing and hedging.

Dr. Sofia Reyes:
Thank you, Robert. Technologically, we're advancing next-generation propulsion, including scramjets for Dark Eagle and adaptive engines for NGAD/GCAP. Our Mojave tests show 30% better thermal performance, and AI/ML in ATLAS computing reduces SWaP by 40% for F-35 Block 4. HELIOS lasers are in LRIP, and autonomy stacks for CCA loyal wingmen hit TRL-6 milestones. These give us a sharp competitive edge.

Mark Donovan:
Thank you, Sofia. Strategically, we're evaluating acquisitions like our $320 million gallium nitride foundry and a pending $1.2 billion directed energy firm to complement our portfolio and expand reach. New models target hypersonics ($15 billion CHGB market), space LEO, and autonomy, with JVs in Turkey/India for offsets and 15% emerging market growth.

Laura Jenkins:
Thank you, Mark. Marketing-wise, our new campaign on resilient defense tech is gaining traction, with digital channels boosting awareness 25% among NATO and Indo-Pacific customers. Results include 32% higher lead conversion and strengthened brand in hypersonics and sustainment.

Operator:
Thank you. We will now begin the question and answer session. Our first question comes from Ben Smith with JPMorgan. Please go ahead.

Ben Smith:
Good morning. Can you provide more color on the major new contract awards, especially international diversification?

David Larson:
Certainly, Ben. As Emily detailed, the $12.4 billion haul included strong FMS growth to 22%, with UAE co-production and Australia AUKUS deals reducing U.S. concentration. These multi-year fixed-price wins with escalators position us well for sustained awards amid global budget rises.

Operator:
Our next question comes from Lisa Green with Goldman Sachs. Please go ahead.

Lisa Green:
Hi, thanks. I'm curious about the commercial aircraft delivery recovery trajectory and supply chain risks?

Emily Carter:
Lisa, deliveries hit 142 in Q3, on pace for 520-570 yearly, with narrowbodies exceeding 2019 rates. We've dual-sourced 80% forgings, stabilizing titanium post-Ukraine, and automation cuts cycles significantly. Backlog $528 billion gives pricing power, though China certs defer some to H2.

Operator:
Our next question comes from Tom Lee with Barclays. Please go ahead.

Tom Lee:
Regarding the technology advancements in hypersonics and their integration into priority programs?

Dr. Sofia Reyes:
Tom, our Dark Eagle scramjets and HAWC tests enable Mach 5+ with superior heat dissipation, feeding into $650 million Q3 hypersonics revenue. NGAD autonomy and CCA swarms via DARPA-inspired ML position us for IOC FY25 and $900 million bookings.

Operator:
Our next question comes from Mike Patel with Morgan Stanley. Please go ahead.

Mike Patel:
Question about strategic priorities, particularly M&A and FY25 outlook?

Mark Donovan:
Mike, we're targeting tuck-ins like the gallium nitride deal to hit 25% space revenue by 2026, alongside capex for localization. FY25 revenue $35.5-36.5 billion and EPS $12.50-13.00 reflect backlog conversion, CCA ramps, and 12.2-12.5% margins.

David Larson:
Thank you for your questions. In closing, I'm confident in our ability to navigate the current environment and deliver long-term value to our shareholders. We remain focused on our strategic priorities, operational excellence, innovation, and capital returns in this expanding A&D market.

Sarah Thompson:
Thank you for joining us today. This concludes our Third Quarter Fiscal 2024 Earnings Conference Call. A replay will be available on our investor relations website.

Operator:
This concludes today's conference call. Thank you for participating. You may now disconnect.
